data.title: Sunil Singhania makes a fresh entry in this defence stock
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Building a successful stock portfolio requires a clear investment strategy, well-defined financial goals and a thorough understanding of market dynamics.

As you develop your own approach, you can also draw valuable lessons from the experience and investment philosophies of seasoned market veterans.

Studying their decisions can offer useful insights, but these must be balanced with your own financial objectives, risk appetite and investment horizon.

One such investor is Sunil Singhania, whose investment moves and portfolio choices attract considerable attention.

Sunil Singhania is the founder of Abakkus Asset Manager, an investment management company.

He has a track record of over two decades in equity markets. He played a significant role in building Reliance-Nippon MF into one of India's largest asset management companies (AMCs).

Sunil Singhania has picked up a stake in defence stock Bharat Earth Movers.

According to the latest shareholding pattern for Sept 2026, investor Sunil Singhania now holds a 1.1% stake in the company. His holding is now valued at Rs.1,769 million (m).

He held no stake in the company in the prior quarters.

While the reasons for the hike remain unclear, a few points may explain the decision.

Q1 FY27 has been a big improvement for BEML and the best first quarter the company has had in the last decade or so, with top-line growth of 29%.

This growth was led by a tremendous turnaround in the Rail and Metro segment, which grew by 178%. It was the first time that BEML hit a positive EBITDA ever and the overall loss has gone down by almost 50%.

Improving financials could be one reason Sunil Singhania picked a stake in the company.

The company has a strong order book of more than Rs.16000 crore. According to the management, BEML is looking at an opportunity size of Rs.35000 crore to Rs.40000 crore, mainly led by the Metro and Rail.

In the defence and mining space, BEML has L1 value of around Rs.900 crore worth of tenders.

The company also has a healthy export order book currently at around US$115 million and the management is optimistic it should end the year with an export order book of around US$200 million.

These may be some of the reasons Sunil Singhania picked a stake in the stock.

BEML's future performance will depend on its ability to convert its sizeable order book into timely execution, revenue growth and sustainable profitability.

The sharp improvement in the Rail and Metro segment is encouraging, but the company must show it can maintain this momentum in subsequent quarters.

Progress in defence, mining and exports could provide additional growth opportunities, while new orders may strengthen revenue visibility.

However, tender conversions, project delays, working-capital requirements and execution costs remain important factors to monitor.

In the past week, the BEML stock is up nearly 3%. However, in the last month, the share price has changed very little. In the past year, the share price has lost 5%.

The stock touched its 52-week high of Rs.2,275.75 on 24 October 2025 and its 52-week low of Rs.1,355 on 30 March 2026.

BEML Ltd is a government-owned engineering and manufacturing company established in May 1964. Headquartered in Bengaluru, it operates under the Ministry of Defence, with the Government of India holding a 54.03% stake.

The company manufactures a wide range of products across three business segments: Defence and Aerospace, Mining and Construction, and Rail and Metro. Its products include military vehicles, missile launchers, bulldozers, excavators, mining dump trucks, railway coaches, metro cars and trainsets. BEML has manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru, Kolar Gold Fields, Mysuru and Palakkad.

data.title: A $2,000,000,000,000 fund may lift a self-imposed ban on Western defence stocks; Details here
data.description:
Norway's $2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund, the largest in the world, could soon end its self-imposed ban on investing in Western defence companies that has lasted years.

The fund currently has stakes in around 1.5% of the publicly listed companies globally, making it one of the biggest investors in the global stock market.

Last week, an independent Gjedrem committee submitted a review to Norway's Finance Ministry, which included a recommendation for a radical change to how the fund approaches defence investments. It argued that Norges Bank must be prepared for situations where conflicts escalate into war. The review was ordered in November 2025, after controversy broke out over some disinvestments from some Israeli and US-based firms.

Norges Bank has not invested in western defence companies for years as their current ethical rules prohibit them from making investments in companies such as Airbus, BAE Systems, Boeing, BWX Technologies and Lockheed Martin, as they contribute to the manufacturing of nuclear weapons.

It is not as if the fund does not invest in defence stocks at all. It does have a 2.3% stake in Germany's Rheinmetall, and a 1.5% stake in Leonardo, listed in Italy.

As per the Gjedrem Committee recommendation, although the nuclear weapons criteria should be retained, its scope could change.

The Fund is not to be invested in companies that produce nuclear weapons, unless the company is domiciled in a nuclear-weapon state under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) that is allied with Norway. Several European and American companies that produce components for nuclear weapons can therefore be reincluded.

According to the recommendations, the fund should invest in companies producing weapons that Norway needs for its own defence, and also proposed to remove the requirement for arms manufacturers to be assessed for whether their products are being used by countries in accordance with international humanitarian laws.

Apart from the rising geopolitical risks, the committee believes that given the fund's capital and influence, it was time to reassess the ethical framework.

Norway's oil fund was set up in the 1990s to invest the windfall from the country's oil and gas industry. Investment decisions are made by Norges Bank Investment Management (NBIM), which also holds stake in many Indian listed entities.

In September last year, controversy broke out after the NBIM ordered exiting positions in American machinery manufacturer Caterpillar and five other Israeli banks, which prompted the US state department to retort by saying that it is "very troubled" by the decision of the fund, which, as per them, was based on "illegitimate claims."

The committee also recommended that the Council of Ethics must continue to operate but no longer advise NBIM on taking action over ethical concerns.

Norway's Finance Ministry will now propose a new ethics framework in a white paper during spring, and Norway's parliament is expected to vote on the new proposed framework sometime in mid-2027. Till then, the current guidelines remain in place.

data.title: BOJ may need to tighten faster if inflation beats forecast, IMF says
data.description:
Key points:
  • IMF sees BOJ 'doing the right thing' in normalising policy
  • Japan 'fully committed' to floating exchange rate, IMF says
  • IMF analysis suggests yen moves since mid-2025 not driven by fundamentals
  • Japan must clarify means of funding for spending plans

By Leika Kihara

The Bank of Japan is "doing the right thing" by normalising monetary policy and may need to raise interest rates faster if inflation rises more than expected, a senior International Monetary Fund official told Reuters.

Japan must also clarify how it plans to fund its big spending plans and lay out a medium-term fiscal framework to ease market concerns about fiscal risks, said Krishna Srinivasan, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department.

"I would say that they are doing the right thing at this point," Srinivasan said on the BOJ's efforts to lift its policy rate towards levels deemed neutral to the economy.

"If inflation rises faster than expected, you have to start tightening faster because you don't want inflation expectations to get un-anchored. It's data dependent," he said in an interview on Friday.

The remarks came ahead of the BOJ's key policy meeting later this month, when it could keep rates steady but drop hawkish hints that would reinforce dominant market expectations of a December hike.

Inflationary pressures from the Middle East conflict and brisk AI-demand were among key themes discussed by policymakers gathering for this week's annual IMF meetings in Bangkok.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda, who attended the IMF meetings, said on Friday the central bank will focus on anchoring underlying inflation around its 2% target and won't tolerate any overshoot, stressing anew its resolve to continue raising interest rates.

For Japan, a weak yen adds to factors pushing up inflation by boosting the cost of raw material imports.

Such mounting price pressures prodded the BOJ to raise rates to a 31-year high of 1.25% in September, following a hike in June. Many analysts expect another rate increase by year-end.

Japan also conducted a rare, coordinated intervention with the US on July 31 to prevent the currency's slide to near 40-year lows from destabilising financial markets.

In staff analysis included in its report on Asia's economy, the IMF said a big portion of yen moves since mid-2025 had little to do with fundamental factors such as yield differentials, and instead co-moved with speculative positions in yen futures.

"Japan has a deep foreign exchange market, so as a first line of defense, they have allowed the exchange rate to move," Srinivasan said.

"Bottom line, I would say that the Japanese authorities are fully committed to a freely floating exchange rate. I've had many discussions with them. So I don't doubt that at all," he said when asked if the recent yen intervention was justified.

FISCAL FRAMEWORK NEEDED

Rising global bond yields have also drawn attention at this week's IMF meetings as debt in advanced economies, including Japan, expanded after years of heavy spending.

Markets worry that Japan may add to its already huge debt pile with the administration's big spending plans and a two-year cut to the consumption tax from April next year.

Srinivasan said Japan has in fact seen fiscal consolidation proceed more than any other G7 country since the pandemic due in part to rising tax revenues.

"Markets are concerned about the fiscal risks because of the uncertainty" on how Japan would pay for the fresh spending and tax-cut plans, he said. "Japan also would benefit from having a medium-term fiscal framework."

data.title: IDBI Bank sale: Keep CCEA decision in abeyance pending independent inquiry, says EAS Sarma
data.description:
Former Secretary to government of India EAS Sarma has demanded that Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) decision on October 14 to disinvest government’s and LIC’s holdings in IDBI be kept in abeyance pending an independent inquiry.

The findings should be presented to Parliament, Sarma wrote in his latest letter to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. “I consider this decision to be ill-advised as it involves serious legal implications, gross undervaluation of IDBI’s assets, and a breach of assurance given by government,” he said in the letter shared with businessline.

Sold for a ‘pittance’

Sarma recalled he had raised ‘multiple concerns’ about disinvestment in his previous letter of August 4, citing a ‘highly opaque, non-competitive environment.’ But CCEA has since approved selection of ‘M/s 10955230 Canada Inc., whose parent entity is Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd.,’ as the strategic buyer for IDBI’s disinvestment.

Purchase consideration is ₹52,878 crore for the acquisition of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank Ltd., comprising government’s 30.48 per cen equity shareholding and LIC’s 30.24 per cent. Sarma described this as a ‘pittance.’LIC equity holding is funded by its millions of policyholders. In fairness to them, the government and LIC ought to have displayed a greater sense of prudence before parting with a 60.72 per cent equity holding at such a low price, Sarma said.

data.title: Jio’s $3.2 billion IPO tests Ambani appeal with young Indians
data.description:
For generations of Indians, Reliance Industries Ltd. was their introduction to the stock market. Founder Dhirubhai Ambani drew middle-income savers into shares, building a following that endured for decades.

Nearly fifty years after Reliance went public, his billionaire son Mukesh and grandson Akash are preparing to list the group’s telecom and digital services arm in what is set to be India’s biggest initial public offering. Jio Platforms Ltd. plans to raise about $3.2 billion in the offering, which opens on Oct. 21. The IPO will test how much the Reliance brand still matters to retail investors.

Jio is pitching to a very different market from the one Dhirubhai knew. India now has more than 130 million registered stock-market investors, nearly 40 per cent of them under 30, according to National Stock Exchange of India data. Thousands of stocks, a vast array of mutual funds and other assets compete for their money. Older shareholders regarded Reliance as a stock they could hold for decades. For younger investors, growth, profits and valuation play a bigger role in the investment decision.

Mahendra Chheda, 69, started as a floor trader in the late 1960s before becoming a member of the Bombay Stock Exchange.

“Be it Dhirubhai’s ambition, his quest to create an army of retail investors or the return of capital to shareholders, Reliance set itself miles apart,” he said. His son, Hardik, 44, an equities trader, takes a different view of Jio.

“I will be taking out profit soon after listing,” he said. “Retail investors owe a lot to the Ambanis for popularizing direct stock ownership, but we are now in a different era of financial markets.”

Reliance, under Mukesh’s leadership, has grown from a maker of textiles and chemicals into India’s most valuable company with businesses spanning energy, consumer goods and telecom.

Under Dhirubhai, a first-generation entrepreneur who challenged Mumbai’s entrenched industrial establishment, the company decided to tap thousands of individual investors to help set up his textile empire.

The November 1977 IPO raised ₹2.8 crore and drew about 58,000 investors, with the offering subscribed seven times, according to Reliance’s annual report. It helped fuel what became known as India’s ‘equity cult,’ as more households began buying shares directly. Annual shareholder meetings grew into mass gatherings, including one held at Cooperage Football Ground in south Mumbai in the mid-1980s.

Reliance shares have delivered an annualized average return of about 29 per cent since listing, according to a presentation at a Mumbai roadshow on Thursday. This year, however, the stock has fallen 23 per cent amid a broader selloff in local equities, putting it on track for its worst annual performance since 2011.

Akash, Jio Platforms’ 34-year-old managing director and Mukesh’s eldest son, is leading the company’s listing, his first major Reliance transaction on his own.

Jio had previously been expected to seek a valuation of about ₹11 lakh crore ($116 billion), people familiar with the matter have said. During global roadshows, fund managers questioned why Jio deserved a premium over smaller rival Bharti Airtel Ltd. and how it planned to make money from digital services beyond its core telecom business, Bloomberg reported.

Jio has drawn more than $20 billion in bids, and overseas investors including Fidelity Management & Research, Allianz SE and Capital Group have indicated interest, people familiar with the matter have said.

Even with that demand, Jio will sell shares at ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 apiece, valuing the company at about $108 billion at the top of the range. That puts it at a discount to Bharti Airtel’s $125 billion market value.

Prathamesh Gokhale, 24, said Jio’s growth outlook and valuation matter more to him than the Ambani legacy. He plans to bid for the IPO.

“If I get lucky with an allotment, I will sell half of my holding in the short term for a quick profit and keep the rest for longer-term gains,” he said. He also views Bharti Airtel as an attractive investment.

Gokhale, who is studying accountancy, said limited capital makes it crucial to free up money for other investments.

His approach is common among India IPO investors. A study by the market regulator in 2024 found that retail investors sold 40 per cent of their allotment within a week of listing. When returns topped 20 per cent, they disposed about two-thirds.

They also have more places to put that money. India’s $5 trillion market now includes consumer-tech firms, digital payment companies, and stock exchanges, alongside industrial groups and multinational names that once dominated trading.

Jio disrupted India’s telecom market when it entered a decade ago with cheap 4G data services. The question now is whether it can keep innovating and deliver the next leg of growth, according to Geetanjali Kedia, an investment adviser at SPTulsian.com.

“Investors have become much more discerning,” she said. “Companies need to consistently deliver returns to get their attention and money.”

data.title: Nike Stock Has Been Dismal. Why It's Time to Be Bullish. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Doug Busch

After years of watching Nike's multiyear stock decline, I am turning bullish. Yes, you heard that right.

The athleticwear company has been dogged by product missteps, weakness in China, and an overreliance on lifestyle and discounting, sending the stock down a whopping 79% from its record high in November 2021.

With the brand's enduring global power still intact and the worst of the inventory and channel reset behind it, the risk/reward from here looks meaningfully better than it has in years — particularly as early evidence of progress is emerging under CEO Elliott Hill. From a technical standpoint, there are also early signs that the stock's collapse could finally be reaching a bottom.

Nike remains bogged down by broader headwinds within the consumer discretionary sector, which ranks as the weakest of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors so far this year, based on the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund's 4.5% decline year to date.

Drilling down into industry subgroups, footwear performance has been heavily bifurcated rather than uniformly weak. Outperformers like Crocs, Wolverine World Wide (think Saucony), and Steve Madden have generated strong year-to-date rallies of 46%, 13%, and 13%, respectively. Conversely, Birkenstock, Deckers Outdoor, and Nike have experienced sharp drawdowns in 2026, sliding 12%, 16%, and 40%, respectively.

Despite this group divergence, Nike presents the most compelling risk/reward situation among its peers over a 12-month horizon. To evaluate the technical foundation behind this secular bullish thesis, let's examine the weekly and monthly charts for a longer time horizon.

Looking at Nike stock's weekly chart, price action broke above its 2026 downtrend against peer Under Armour this summer on the ratio chart. The absolute chart continues to reflect long-term overhead resistance after the stock lost its 50-week simple moving average in early 2022. That key moving average has repeatedly capped recovery attempts, generating sharp rejections marked by heavy bearish engulfing weekly candlesticks in December 2023, June and October 2024, and December 2025. Each rejection resulted in declines ranging from 8% to 22% on at least double the average weekly volume.

Despite this prolonged resistance, high-volume capitulation signals indicate a long-term bottoming process is under way. During the week ending Oct. 2, Nike dropped over 5% but printed a long-legged spinning top candle — a classic trend exhaustion signature — on its highest weekly volume in nearly 40 years.

This historic volume spike suggests institutions — rather than retail traders — are accumulating the stock, laying the foundation for a structural recovery. I expect a nice turnaround story going forward, and bulls on this time frame can expect a bounce toward that 50-week SMA near the very round $50 number by mid-2027. That would mark a 35% gain from current prices, and investors can get paid a 4% dividend yield in the interim. Remain bullish above $33.75.

Nike was trading around $37.50 Friday.

Turning to the monthly chart, the stock's severe relative lag against the broader State Street SPDR S&P Retail ETF is evident dating back to late 2021. From an absolute price perspective, the all-time high was capped by a doji candle in November 2021. Subsequent recovery attempts marked by bullish candlestick patterns repeatedly failed over the following years. These included a morning star completed in August 2024, a cluster of three dojis between November 2025 and February 2026, and a harami this past July — all occurring against a backdrop of heavy institutional selling on larger-than-normal volume since June 2024.

However, price action in October could be constructing a major structural turning point. This month, now more than half over, is shaping up to print a bullish hammer supported by historic volume. Trading activity is already tracking as the second-highest monthly volume surge since May 1997, with two full weeks of trading still remaining. This landmark volume offers asymmetric risk/reward across both weekly and monthly time frames.

Doug Busch is the senior technical analyst at Barron's Investor Circle. His technical view is added to stock picks, including those published exclusively for Investor Circle readers. A glossary of technical terms is updated regularly with new entries.

data.title: Urban Company's Loss Triples to 183cr
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: Home services platform Urban Company posted a net loss of 183 crore for the July-September period, up over threefold from 59 crore in Q2FY26. The ballooning of the company's loss happened on the back of elevated spending to compete in the buzzy instant househelp business.

For the second quarter of this fiscal, operating revenue grew 41% year-on-year to 537 crore. The company's board, on October 16, also approved a plan to raise 2,500 crore. When the company went public in September 2025, it had raised 472 crore. Urban Company's cofounder and CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal, speaking at the post earnings analyst call, said that InstaHelp's losses will remain elevated for many quarters to come. "We are building for scale, not near-term profits," he said, adding that from Q3FY28, its core business profits will fund InstaHelp losses.

On the proposed fundraise, Bhal said, "Should the competitive intensity in InstaHelp rise, we have both the balance sheet and the intent to respond in full." In a letter to shareholders, the Gurugram-based company said it had 1,901 crore in cash as of September 30, while its businesses excluding the InstaHelp segment generated 119 crore in adjusted Ebitda over the past nine months. "The purpose of the raise is flexibility. The business today is materially larger than at the time of listing, and growth has stepped up meaningfully.

We now operate three businesses at scale, with proven economics across India Core, International and Native," the company said. "The raise gives us the ability to invest with conviction across each of these areas: to sustain higher growth in the core business, to fund the next phase of growth in Native, to cement leadership in InstaHelp through its most competitive phase, and to pursue inorganic opportunities selectively," it added.

Urban Company reported a 41% year-on-year rise in operating revenue to 537 crore for the July-September quarter. Its net loss, however, tripled to 175 crore as continued cash burn in InstaHelp weighed on its bottom line. InstaHelp under pressure With competition in the instant househelp segment remaining intense, Urban Company's post-discount average order value (AOV) fell to 118 in the September quarter from 134 in the June quarter. "Competitive intensity remained high, and we leaned further into new user acquisition, where introductory pricing is lower," the company said in the letter. "We regard this as the cost of building habit while the category is being formed, not as the steady-state price of the service.

In the medium term, we believe net order value should move up for us, albeit slowly and subject to competitive intensity. As it does, loss per order should improve further," it added. Urban Company competes with Nexus Venture Partners-backed Snabbit and General Catalyst-backed Pronto in the instant househelp segment.

data.title: Online Push, Strong Product Portfolio May Help Nestle India Sustain Growth
data.description:
Snehal Mergu ET Intelligence Group: Nestle India's strong double-digit year-on-year revenue and profit growth in the September quarter has failed to enthuse investors as the company's commentary on input cost inflation and a sequential margin squeeze have weakened the market sentiment.

The stock has lost nearly 9% in two trading sessions after the firm declared its September quarter numbers. This has brought down its P/E at 59, below the five-year average multiple of 73. While long-term investors may look for a buying opportunity given the strong sales volume momentum and market penetration, short-term investors may have to look somewhere else for quick gains.

Although Nestle India posted a healthy 20.3% rise in revenue and a 35.9% jump in net profit, the company flagged continued inflation in key commodities, particularly cocoa. Coffee and wheat prices may remain range-bound, while sugar and edible oils have stabilised at elevated levels, and milk remains firm but may ease as supply improves.

Despite 46% rise in marketing spends, Ebitda margin expanded to 23.8% in September quarter from 22% a year ago. It, however, contracted by 40 basis points sequentially. Given rising advertising spend and commodity cost inflation, analysts expect limited room for further margin expansion year-on-year. The volume-led growth story remains intact given broad-based demand across categories and supported by market-share gains, premiumisation and deeper distribution.

The company continues to benefit from rapid expansion of quick-commerce and ecommerce channels. JM Financial Institutional Securities believes Nestle India's strong performance over the past four to five quarters has been driven by GST rate rationalisation and company-led initiatives such as distribution expansion, premiumisation and innovation.

While sales growth is expected to moderate in H2 of FY27 from elevated levels seen in first half, the brokerage believes this reflects a higher base rather than a deterioration in company's underlying fundamentals. It said Nestle's strong brand portfolio and pricing power equip it to navigate commodity-cost volatility and sustain healthy growth over medium term.

Analysts have largely retained 'buy' recommendations on stock despite trimming target prices by 7-17%. Even after cuts, revised targets imply a potential upside of 9-19% from Friday's closing price of 1,265, suggesting brokerages remain constructive on company's long-term growth prospects. Sustaining volume growth and festive-season demand may be key monitorables.

data.title: IGX Gets Nod for LNG Capacity Booking Platform
data.description: Our Bureau New Delhi: Indian Gas Exchange (IGX) has received regulatory approval to set up a capacity booking platform for liquefied natural gas (LNG) import terminals, enabling users to access terminal capacity more easily and transparently, the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) said in a statement on Friday. "The proposed platform will provide a centralised and organised mechanism for the listing and booking of unutilised regasification capacity at LNG terminals, enabling market participants to identify available capacity and access it in accordance with their requirements," PNGRB said. "It is notable that a large number of terminals are reporting poor capacity utilisation and could avail of this facility to attract LNG cargoes by transparently discovering lower regasification charges," it added. At present, terminals enter into bilateral agreements with users for capacity booking. The IGX platform will offer an additional route to book capacity, with voluntary participation.

data.title: Apex Court Upholds Forensic Audit in Daiichi-Fortis Case
data.description:
Indu Bhan New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed appeals by DCB Bank and UBS Management Services India challenging a Delhi High Court order directing a forensic audit of transactions linked to hospital chain Fortis Healthcare (FHL) in connection with Daiichi Sankyo's arbitration case. A bench led by chief justice Surya Kant reiterated that the audit ordered by the high court on August 31 was confined to the transactions among FHL, its holding company Fortis Healthcare (FHHPL), and former promoters Malvinder Singh and Shivinder Singh.

It clarified that this did not mean there would be a "fishing and roving enquiry" into the affairs of the banks. The banks' role in the audit is only "incidental" and meant to assist the process, it added. DCB Bank and UBS (formerly Credit Suisse Finance India) argued that the Japanese drugmaker had told the high court that it did not want a forensic audit of the banks.

They also submitted that they had neither invoked any pledges nor sold any shares and that they were neither parties to the 2016 arbitral award nor were made parties to the execution proceedings by Daiichi. Besides, no allegations or findings were made against them to mandate a forensic audit, they said. On September 29, the top court had dismissed similar appeals by YES Bank and Axis Bank.

data.title: Tata Motors CV's Bid Gets Iveco Shareholders' Nod
data.description:
APPROVALS FOLLOW INCREASE IN OFFER PRICE Our Bureau Mumbai: Commercial vehicle maker Tata Motors said Friday that shareholders of Iveco Group have approved all resolutions of its board on the Indian automaker's voluntary public tender offer for the Italian truck and bus maker, marking a key step towards completing the acquisition.

The approvals follow an increase in the offer price by Tata Motors on October 9. Shareholders, at an extraordinary general meeting in Amsterdam, approved resolutions relating to the offer by TML CV Holdings, acting through it, for all issued ordinary shares of Iveco.

Tata Motors announced the 3.8 billion acquisition of Iveco's commercial vehicle business in July 2025. The deal excludes the defence business, which Iveco agreed to sell separately to Italy's Leonardo.

Tata Motors will also acquire Exor's 27.06% stake in Iveco as part of the transaction. The tender offer opened at 14.10 per share before being raised to 14.40 on October 9. The revised offer was declared final, with the offer period scheduled to close October 26.

Resolutions approved at Friday's meeting include amendments to Iveco's articles of association, which will take effect upon settlement of the offer, and its conversion from a publicly listed limited liability company into a private limited liability company. The latter change will take effect after delisting, at a time determined by the offeror.

Shareholders also approved a proposed demerger after the offer is completed, which the offeror can implement if it acquires about 80% of Iveco's ordinary shares, among other conditions. A subsequent sale of shares was approved, subject to implementation of the demerger. The resolutions further provide for Iveco's eventual dissolution and the appointment of a liquidator and a custodian for its books and records should the demerger and liquidation proceed. The meeting also approved the appointment of board members who will take office upon settlement of the offer. Iveco's outgoing board members were granted discharge for their tenure immediately preceding the settlement.

data.title: Starlink Entry Welcome, No Fear of Competition: Reliance
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: Reliance Industries (RIL) doesn't fear competition from other satellite communications providers, but all players, including US-based Starlink, must comply with Indian laws, the Mukesh Ambani-owned company said Friday.

In a statement responding to "recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market", the company said its own satellite services are awaiting government approvals. "That openness rests on the rule of law," RIL said. "As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign.

Jio's own satellite services await clearances." Reliance explicitly welcomed Starlink's participation in India's satellite communications market, while calling for compliance with the country's regulatory framework. "We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink," it said. "Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land." RIL said India's openness to investment and innovation, both domestic and international, has supported the growth of Indian enterprises, including its own. "At Reliance, we have never feared competition," it said. "We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best." Reliance pointed to Jio's entry into India's crowded telecom market in 2016, saying the company had started without a single customer and built a base of more than 530 million customers over a decade.

It said Jio had given Indians some of the world's best digital infrastructure and most affordable data. RIL's statement comes days after SpaceX founder Elon Musk alleged that "unnamed oligarchs" were blocking Starlink's entry into India.

In a scathing post on X last week, Musk wrote: "Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people.This is a crime against the people of India!" Later, the communications ministry said that satellite communication operators must demonstrate compliance with security conditions before moving to the next step of seeking spectrum assignment.

OneWeb India Communications, Jio Satellite Communications and Starlink Satellite Communications are the three companies that have been granted unified licences with authorisation for Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite (GMPCS) services. Bhartsi Airtel chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said earlier this week that his satcom venture, Eutelsat OneWeb, is awaiting Indian government clearances to start operations.

data.title: Panasonic Reverses Stand on Indianising Top Deck, Offers Key Roles to Expats
data.description:
Ratna Bhushan & Writankar Mukherjee New Delhi | Kolkata: Panasonic has rejigged its top deck in India, appointing expats from its Japanese headquarters to key roles in a reversal of a strategy initiated five years ago to bring more operations under Indian leadership.

Kazuki Sato has been named executive director at flagship entity Panasonic Life Solutions India in the most recent leadership appointment. He will be based in Gurugram. Other recent appointments include Yoshiyuki Kato as managing director and chief executive officer, and Hirokazu Kamoda, who has been heading the AC division, as deputy managing director. "Panasonic has been restructured as an expat-led organisation now, with the top deck being led primarily by executives from its headquarters," an executive close to the developments said.

A Panasonic Life Solutions India spokesperson, in an email response, said Sato will "focus on strengthening the company's support structure across India, laying the groundwork to enable future business expansion." The spokesperson confirmed that Kato is heading the India business and said Kamoda has been assigned additional responsibility of deputy managing director to deepen cross-functional synergy.

The Japanese appliances and consumer electronics maker's former India chairman Manish Sharma had stepped down last November after more than a decade-long stint. Another company veteran, Sandeep Sehgal also quit as director and head of sales at Panasonic Life Solutions India. He has since joined rival Havells India as executive vice president (sales) for its Lloyd's business.

Panasonic's India unit exited the refrigerator and washing machine segments and cut headcount by over 10% to focus only on air-conditioners mid last year, citing a global restructuring aimed at exiting loss-making businesses worldwide. Both refrigerator and washing machine businesses in India failed to keep pace with aggressive competition from Indian and Korean rivals such as Voltas, Samsung and LG. "All operations have been downsized, and the company is undergoing natural attrition," the executive mentioned above said. "While there are no further layoffs right now, the staff strength has been reduced to about half." The company spokesperson said the recent top-level appointments "reflect a deliberate strategy to combine strong business leadership with robust organisational support as the company pursues its long-term growth road map in the country." It has also halved the size of its corporate headquarter in Gurugram in line with the reduction in headcount.

Panasonic Life Solutions India in July this year said its residential air conditioner business grew 50% year-on-year in the summer. The company's FY25 sales stood at 11,500 crore, with a net profit of 1,100 crore. Boston Consulting Group and the Confederation of Indian Industry estimated in a report last month that India's consumer durables market could touch sales of 3.25 lakh crore by year 2030, growing 8-10%, which it said was on the back of increased household incomes, easier financing, premiumisation and replacement demand. At the current pace of localisation, a large part of this projections could still be met through imports, the report said.

data.title: Peak Power Demand Exceeded 250 GW Through Most of Sept
data.description:
Shilpa Samant New Delhi: Peak domestic power demand is sustaining record highs for September, exceeding 250 GW, on most days, close to the levels seen in summer. Demand reached 250 GW Thursday, fuelled by cooling and irrigation needs. India's power sector planner recently said the country will require additional base load through conventional sources such as thermal power plants to meet the strong demand, along with renewable energy sources.

Power consumption in September rose around 11% driven by cooling and irrigation requirements amid below-normal monsoon rainfall. October, when demand tends to start falling with the onset of cooler months, saw its highest-ever peak power demand met at 260 GW on October 5. Only a few days in the month, this demand figure fell below 240 GW. "Demand is expected to reduce next week with lower pressure on cooling appliances and irrigation," a government official told ET. Electricity prices in the day-ahead market of the Indian Energy Exchange are hovering above 7 a unit so far this month.

Coal stocks at power plants, which fell sharply as heavy rains in coal-bearing regions hit production and supply, are currently at around 18 million tonnes. Coal stocks at domestic coal-based power plants fell to 17.9 million tonnes as of October 15 from 18.2 million tonnes on October 10 and 18.5 million tonnes as of October 1. Plants using imported coal have 2.4 million tonnes of inventory.

data.title: Urban Company's Q2 Loss Triples to 183 cr on InstaHelp Biz Burn
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: Home services platform Urban Company has reported a quarterly net loss of 183 crore, weighed down by higher spending to compete in the instant house-help segment. The company said its InstaHelp business would continue to incur elevated losses for several quarters.

For the September quarter, the company's net loss was more than three times the 59 crore loss recorded a year ago, according to the results declared on Friday. Gurgaon-based Urban Company competes with Nexus Venture Partners-backed Snabbit and General Catalyst-backed Pronto in the instant househelp segment.

Urban Company's operating revenue during the quarter stood at 537 crore, up by 41% from a year ago. The company's board, on October 16, also approved a plan to raise 2,500 crore. Urban Company had raised 472 crore through a public offering of shares in September 2025.

At the post-earnings analyst call, cofounder and chief executive officer Abhiraj Singh Bhal said InstaHelp's losses will remain elevated for many quarters to come. "We are building for scale, not near-term profits," he said, adding that from the third quarter of FY28, its core business profits will fund InstaHelp losses. On the proposed fundraise, Bhal said, "Should the competitive intensity in InstaHelp rise, we have both the balance sheet and the intent to respond in full." In a letter to shareholders, Urban Company said it had 1,901 crore in cash as of September 30, while its businesses, excluding the InstaHelp segment, generated 119 crore in adjusted EBITDA over the last nine months.

data.title: Ather Insurance Gets IRDAI Approval to Distribute Policies
data.description:
Our Bureau Bengaluru: Electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy's wholly owned subsidiary Ather Insurance has received regulatory approval to distribute and service insurance policies, as the company looks to diversify revenue and generate recurring income from its existing customer base.

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India granted the subsidiary a certificate of registration on October 15 to act as a corporate agent (composite), Ather Energy said in a stock exchange filing on Thursday. The registration covers life, general and health insurance.

The approval is for insurance distribution and servicing, rather than underwriting policies. Ather, in its filings, said the move would diversify its revenue streams. It did not disclose insurer partnerships or quantify the revenue it expects from the business. The registration remains valid from October 15, subject to payment of an annual fee, unless suspended or cancelled by the regulator, according to the filing.

Ather ranked third in India's electric two-wheeler market in September, with 30,479 registrations and a 14.71% share, according to Vahan data. TVS Motor led with 26.06%, followed by Bajaj Auto at 23.36%. Ola Electric had a 6.49% share. For FY25, Ather reported revenue from operations of 2,255 crore, up about 29% from 1,753.8 crore a year earlier. The company's net loss narrowed to 812.3 crore from 1,059.7 crore. Scooter sales rose 42% to 155,394 units from 109,577 in FY24. Non-vehicle sales accounted for 12% of revenue in FY25, compared with 10% a year earlier. In August, Ather launched the Konarc, its first mass-market electric scooter, priced at Rs 1 lakh and aimed at entry-level models such as the TVS iQube and Bajaj Chetak.

data.title: Major development banks step up support for critical minerals value chains
data.description:
Multilateral development banks (MDBs) will strengthen efforts to help mineral-rich developing economies add more value to their resources by moving beyond extraction into processing, refining and manufacturing, according to an outline of a critical minerals collaboration framework published on Saturday.

  • The banks involved include the World Bank, the African Development Bank, the Asian Development Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank, according to the outline

  • The October framework calls for coordinated support across critical mineral supply chains, including financing, infrastructure and policy aimed at creating jobs, boosting domestic value addition, attracting private investment and supporting low-carbon transition

  • MDBs plan to support mineral corridors incorporating power, transport, logistics, water and digital infrastructure, while strengthening project preparation and using co-financing, guarantees and other financing tools to mobilise capital and accelerate private sector investments

  • They will also seek closer alignment on environmental and social standards, coordinate support to governments and better connect mining projects with infrastructure and industrial development

  • An MDB working group will coordinate implementation of the framework's objectives and report annually to the Heads of MDBs Group on progress

data.title: BlackRock sells $71.78 million in Bitcoin as ETF redemptions pile up
data.description:
BlackRock has sold $71.78 million worth of Bitcoin, according to a widely shared post on X. That number sounds dramatic when you attach the name of the world's largest asset manager to it.

The reality is more mundane, and arguably more telling. The selling traces back to investors pulling money out of BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), not to Larry Fink's team deciding Bitcoin had a bad vibe.

IBIT is the largest US spot Bitcoin ETF, holding tens of billions of dollars in assets. When shareholders redeem, the fund sells some of the Bitcoin backing those shares to pay them out.

BlackRock has made that point itself. The firm maintains its Bitcoin sales are purely reactive, driven by client demand, and no proprietary Bitcoin selling by BlackRock has been documented. Every sale on record ties back to redemptions.

The $71.78 million figure lands amid a run of similar moves. Research covering mid-October 2026 shows IBIT clients sold approximately $65.4 million in Bitcoin on October 13, 2026.

That followed a much rougher session earlier in the month. On October 7, 2026, IBIT saw $207.7 million in outflows in a single day.

IBIT was not alone that day. Net outflows across all US spot Bitcoin ETFs hit $484.9 million on October 7, which means BlackRock's fund accounted for a sizable slice of the exodus.

Zoom out to the full week, and the picture gets bleaker. Combined outflows from Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF products exceeded $1.2 billion, marking the weakest stretch for these funds since late June 2026.

Bitcoin has been trading in a range of roughly $80,000 to $83,000 during this period. The redemptions have coincided with price swings around that band.

Higher rates matter here for a simple reason. When safe assets start paying more, the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset like Bitcoin goes up.

Since launching in January 2024, IBIT has become the default on-ramp for institutions that want Bitcoin exposure without touching a private key.

There is also precedent for large holders trimming positions. Harvard Management reduced its IBIT stake by about $72 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, another case where the selling started with the client, not the issuer.

Framing these flows as "BlackRock sells Bitcoin" makes for a punchy post. It also implies a strategic call by the firm, which the evidence does not support.

BlackRock is acting as a pass-through here. The Bitcoin it sells belongs, functionally, to IBIT shareholders who decided they wanted dollars instead.

What the data actually shows is a sentiment problem among the fund's clients. And for anyone tracking Bitcoin's price, client sentiment may matter more than BlackRock's corporate opinion anyway.

ETF flows have become one of the clearest real-time windows into institutional appetite for Bitcoin. When money pours in, funds buy. When it pours out, they sell, and that selling hits the spot market.

Still, flow data is noisy. One heavy day, like the $207.7 million IBIT saw on October 7, can be followed by smaller outflows or even inflows once markets settle. The October 13 figure of approximately $65.4 million was meaningfully smaller than that early-month spike.

For BlackRock, the stakes are reputational as much as financial. Its insistence that it only follows client demand is part of what makes IBIT credible to cautious institutions.

data.title: IDBI Bank Stake Sale: Government cites 2018 court ruling to defend disinvestment
data.description:
The government on Saturday, October 17, reiterated that it has the legal authority to dilute or divest its shareholding in IDBI Bank, citing a 2018 Delhi High Court ruling that held there was no provision in the law preventing it from reducing its stake in the lender.

In a clarification issued by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the government said an amendment seeking to restrict dilution of its stake was proposed during parliamentary discussions on the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, but was rejected and did not form part of the enacted legislation.

The clarification comes after the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved the strategic sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings for ₹52,878.08 crore on Wednesday.

The transaction comprises the government's 30.48% stake and Life Insurance Corporation of India's (LIC) 30.24% holding.

What the Delhi High Court said

The government cited the Delhi High Court's December 17, 2018, judgment in All India IDBI Officers' Association v. Union of India & Others, which dismissed a petition challenging the dilution of the government's shareholding.

The court held that statements made during parliamentary debates could not override the legislation ultimately enacted by Parliament. It also ruled that the doctrine of promissory estoppel could not be invoked to prevent the government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Bank.

“There is no ambiguity in the language of the IDBI Repeal Act, 2003 and there is no scope to read any provision into the said enactment which proscribes the Government from reducing or divesting its stake in IDBI Ltd,” the court said.

The doctrine of promissory estoppel generally prevents a party from going back on a promise when another party has relied on it to their detriment. The court, however, held that statements made during parliamentary debates did not amount to a representation that could restrict the government's ability to dilute its stake.

Government cites earlier Budget announcements

The PIB also pointed to successive Union Budget speeches that outlined the government's policy on transforming IDBI Bank and reducing its ownership.

In the 2016-17 Budget, then Finance Minister Arun Jaitley said the government would take forward the bank's transformation and consider reducing its stake to below 50%.

In the 2021-22 Budget, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman listed IDBI Bank among the entities targeted for strategic disinvestment and said legislative amendments would be required for the proposed privatisation of public sector banks and a general insurance company.

The government said the legislative history, the High Court's ruling and successive Budget announcements collectively demonstrate the evolution of its policy towards IDBI Bank's strategic disinvestment.

Fairfax deal to transfer management control

Under the approved transaction, the government will retain a 15% stake in IDBI Bank, while LIC will hold 19%, taking their combined ownership to 34%. However, neither the government nor LIC will have board representation after the transaction, according to the approved restructuring framework.

Fairfax's winning bid of ₹81 per share was above the independently determined benchmark valuation of ₹75.99 per share. The transaction is set to become India's largest foreign direct investment deal in the financial services sector.

The restructuring framework also envisages a resolution of Fairfax's existing holding of around 40% in CSB Bank, with a merger with IDBI Bank or an exit from CSB Bank being the routes under consideration, in view of Reserve Bank of India norms on promoter ownership in multiple banks.

The government has also empowered the Alternative Mechanism to undertake future minority stake sales of its residual holding through the open market, while LIC will manage its remaining stake in accordance with regulatory requirements.
